findings.text: — §10 requires both "a state write to a plan whose impl is derived removes the authored `plan-impl` meta" and "a no-change parse and serialise stays byte-identical, so a reader-only pass never touches the file", but the write path it names, `write_state` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:2219`), takes only `(html_text, state)` and is a pure text transform with no notion of whether a write changes state; the no-op protection in production lives in the caller instead, `serve.py:3913`'s state-dict comparison with `version`/`modified` stripped, which skips the disk write for a patch carrying no content change. An implementer reading §10 in isolation can therefore only key removal on the meta disagreeing with the served figure — which fires on a no-change parse and serialise too and makes case (b) unsatisfiable on the stale-meta fixture the section describes — or invent a signal the plan does not specify, most plausibly comparing the incoming `version` with the file's existing `plan-version` meta. The section also names no caller at all, where §8 names `edit_plan` and §9 names `_replayed_response`. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: without the entry point and the detection rule named, the node either strips the meta on a reader-only serialise (the churn §10 explicitly forbids) or invents a gate, and case (b)'s "that plan" is ambiguous between the stale-meta fixture and the post-removal plan, so the requirement it is meant to pin is not pinned.
